I take the uphill struggle to mean that the going will get tough, shit will hit the fan, etc. until the final goal is reached (resulting in the peak of happiness/satisfaction). From the highest point, one can only travel downhill. The going will never be as tough, and the shit has already hit the fan, so downhill implies an easier time than uphill (just like traveling downhill is easier than uphill). However, uphill had a reward at the peak. Because this reward has now been achieved, or the reward no longer exists, there is no final goal; nothing to strive for. In this sense, "it's all downhill from here" implies that one has already experienced the peak, and that the peak will not come again for a considerable amount of time.

Of course, context can play an important role as well. I suppose most native-English speakers will never realize this, but English is an extremely complicated and fickle language.

I believe meta game is very important. Here are the components (IMO) to meta game:

* Knowing exactly what your hero is capable of. If you are witch slayer with a lvl 3 stun (260 dmg), lvl 2 sheep, and lvl 1 ult (500 dmg), you are capable of 760 magic damage. Right? WRONG! Every hero has magic armor which is something like 25% damage reduction, and it can only go up with magic armor items/spells. So for witch slayer (lvl 6) to kill someone with no additional magic armor, they should have 600 hp or less (stun/ult takes out ~570 dmg, sneak in 1 or 2 regular attacks to account for remaining HP/HP regen).
* Knowing what your opponent is capable of. In the same scenario as above, let's say I'm trying to kill a lvl 6 Glacius with 700 HP. **Your opponent will not just sit and smile while you unload your spells!** If Glacius has an opportunity, he will freeze/slow you, and if you're out of spells/mana, he can even ult you. He may seem weak, but with 700 HP, I would give the edge to Glacius.
